answer.evidence: The stair flight repeats a pattern of a tread band (rows 22-25, 30-34, 39-43) that ends in a light front-edge line (rows 26, 35, 44). Dark shadow rows follow each edge line (27-29, 36-38, 45-46), and a vertical riser/front face sits below. The treads are 4-5 rows deep and the red carpet runs over them. The dark arch at the top (rows 3-14) is a recess rather than a main volume. The steps therefore read as top surfaces with front faces, which is three-quarter view.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a stone-arch stair niche with a red carpet runner. It has about 5 stone steps (highlight, light, mid, dark, deep) with brick-like block edges and stepped risers, which is comparable to the references' 5 steps. Its 11 visible tones per tile sit between window2 (7) and door2 (15). Near-flat coverage is 19%, higher than the references' 1% and 9%, but the candidate is small and the flat areas are the dark interior and the carpet, not large stone faces. Its dark edge pixels are only 13% neutral, so the outlines lean toward the tint of the adjacent material (brown and red-brown), whereas the references are fully neutral. That is the opposite of the sticker look. Texture is moderate: stone block lines and carpet bands are present, but there is less grain than on the door. Overall it would sit acceptably next to the references, though it is slightly lower in density than the door.
